As pointed out by @marco66colombo in #1412, pytest 9 enforces a rule that fixtures can't be parametrized. The way around that is indirect parametrization via the calling test function. This PR makes that change for all tests. 

Downsides:
- Nested parametrizations are not supported this way, leading to a bit of overhead in declaring tests.
- The tests are no longer named using the values of the parameters, so a test will no longer by called `test_embedding_accuracy[Catapult, io_parallel]` but rather `test_embedding_accuracy[hls_model3]` for example. This will make it more annoying to identify the failing test.

- Internal GDPR-compliant messaging

author: derekkraan
body:
Hi,

First of all thanks for the great library, this has really been helping us get our use case off the ground.

We started running into an issue where Chrome didn't want to set the remote description, failing with a message like "Failed to set SSL role for the transport".

The full scenario is that the server initializes the initial (voice-only) connection. Then, when the user is ready to share their screen, the user initiates an offer to the server that includes the video track. The server responds with an answer, which Chrome refuses to apply. In the same scenario, Firefox _does_ apply the answer.

Doing some investigation, I came to understand that when there is an existing DTLS connection, Chrome does not tolerate switching roles, while Firefox does. So, even though the RFC mandates `a=setup:actpass` in the offer, Chrome doesn't accept `a=setup:active` in the answer, since in the already-established connection, Chrome is active and the server is passive.

The proposed solution is to track the dtls role, and continue to respond with the same role, as initially established.

In my limited testing, this appears to work with both Chrome and Firefox.

# BUG-004 — Affichage des dates en français et timezone Europe/Paris

**Statut** : ✅ Résolu  

---

## Problème identifié

Les dates des articles étaient affichées en anglais, au format américain (MM/DD/YYYY) et avec la timezone américaine (America/Los_Angeles).  
Cela provoquait un affichage incorrect pour les utilisateurs français et une incohérence avec les dates stockées en base.

La cause était une configuration par défaut de Laravel en anglais avec une timezone US, ainsi qu’un formatage côté frontend utilisant `en-US`.

---

## Solution implémentée

La correction a été appliquée sur deux niveaux :

### Backend (Laravel)
- La locale a été définie sur `fr`
- La timezone a été définie sur `Europe/Paris`
- Carbon a été configuré pour utiliser le français

### Frontend (React)
- Les dates sont maintenant formatées avec `fr-FR`
- La timezone `Europe/Paris` est utilisée pour l’affichage

Les dates restent stockées en **UTC** dans la base de données, ce qui respecte les bonnes pratiques.

---

## Tests effectués

- [x] Les dates s’affichent en français  
- [x] Le format est **JJ/MM/AAAA**  
- [x] L’heure correspond à la timezone **Europe/Paris**  
- [x] Les dates en base n’ont pas été modifiées  

---

## Résumé

> L’affichage des dates a été corrigé en alignant la locale et la timezone côté backend et frontend, tout en conservant les données stockées en UTC.

---

## Checklist

- [x] Backend configuré en français  
- [x] Frontend formatant les dates correctement  
- [x] Tests manuels validés  
- [x] Ticket BUG-004 résolu

### Introduction

Here we add the v6.0.0 upgrade handler that will be executed on testnet and mainnet. Based on https://github.com/mezo-org/mezod/compare/v5.0.0...main, the breaking change that requires action in the upgrade handler is bumping the version of `Maintenance` precompile to expose the setter and getter for the precompile calls limit.

Tentative plan is to execute this upgrade as follows:
- Testnet: On block `10325250` which is expected on January 20, around 10:00 UTC (11:00 CET)
- Mainnet: To be determined

### Changes

Did the necessary changes as described in [upgrades.md](https://github.com/mezo-org/mezod/blob/main/docs/upgrades.md#planned-upgrade-with-chain-halt)

### Testing

1. Checkout the v5.0.0 tag currently used on testnet and mainnet.
2. Spin up a fresh localnet using `make localnet-bin-clean && make localnet-bin-init`.
3. Start at least three nodes using `make localnet-bin-start`.
4. Make sure you cannot call `setMaxPrecompilesCallsPerExecution/getMaxPrecompilesCallsPerExecution` on the `Maintenance` precompile.
5. Get PoA owner address using `npx hardhat validatorPool:owner` from `precompile/hardhat`.

7. Wait until the upgrade block. Nodes should stop consensus and ask for an upgrade.
8. Switch to this PR's branch (`v6-upgrade-handler`) and stop all your nodes. 
9. Run `make build`.
10. Restart your nodes.
11. They should print "running v6.0.0 upgrade handler" and start producing blocks after a short while.
12. Ensure the features enabled in the upgrade handler work - methods mentioned in point 4 should be now callable.

body:
When running glibc tests under user mode NFS, tst-syslog was causing a hang. The hang was traced to unfsd exitting with a buffer overflow being detected.

This was traced down to mksocket() where we'd see:

socket path '/media/build/poky/build/build-st-2118464/tmp/work/x86-64-v3-poky-linux/glibc-testsuite/2.42+git/build-x86_64-poky-linux/testroot.root/dev/log' is too long at 141 vs 108

There is a length check in mknod_args() but obj may not be setup at this point by cat_name() since the functions can be executed out of order according to C.

To avoid this, make the order explict. This means the length is checked and we avoid the buffer overflow.

- The status only served to indicate "this task is in the process of restarting" but functionally behaved identically to `running` with a `restart` command
- Once the new container starts, it transitions to `running` anyway

body: ## Summary Replaces the internal `http` workflow step with a new workflows-specific `http` connector, preserving the existing step interface while enabling connector-backed HTTP execution. Issue: * https://github.com/elastic/security-team/issues/15301 ## Context Workflows currently expose an internal `http` step type that allows arbitrary HTTP requests to be executed directly from workflow definitions. This implementation is self-contained and bypasses the connector framework. The goal is to support HTTP requests backed by connectors in order to gain: * Secure secret and credential management * Reusability across workflows * Centralized configuration (e.g. base URL, authentication, default headers) At the same time, we want to avoid introducing breaking changes to existing workflows. ## Why introduce a new `.http` connector The internal `http` step solves parameter flexibility, but comes with significant drawbacks: * No secret or credential management * Authentication details must be embedded directly in workflow definitions * No reuse or centralized configuration We considered extending the webhook connector to support dynamic parameters, but rejected this option due to its widespread usage across other teams and products, and the risk of introducing behavioral changes or additional complexity outside of workflows. Instead, this PR introduces a new workflows-specific `http` connector, derived from the `webhook` connector implementation but designed to: * Allow dynamic request parameters at execution time * Leverage the connector framework for secrets and credentials * Transparently replace the internal `http` step (same step signature), avoiding breaking changes This effectively migrates workflows from an internal HTTP implementation to a connector-backed model while maintaining backward compatibility. ### Screenshots No available from the stack connectors creation flow: Connector creation flow available from within Workflows: #### Configuration: #### Usage: With `connector-id`. ### Description

This PR adds support for controlling depth buffer writes in material definitions. The new `depthWrite` property allows developers to specify whether a material should write to the depth buffer during rendering.

This is particularly useful for transparent objects that shouldn't occlude other geometry behind them. When `depthWrite` is set to `false`, transparent materials can render correctly without blocking objects that should be visible through them.

**Changes:**
- Added `depthWrite?: boolean` property to `MaterialDefinition` type with default value of `true`
- Implemented `depthWrite` handling in `MaterialManager` when creating materials (defaults to `true` if not specified)
- Added `depthWrite` support in highlight definition merging logic
- Updated documentation to clarify the relationship between `depthTest` and `depthWrite`

### Additional context

This feature complements the existing `depthTest` property and provides finer control over depth buffer operations.

## Documentation

- Quick setup commands (`bash scripts/setup.sh`)
- Automation coverage matrix (what's automated vs. manual)
- Validation workflow invocation (`gh workflow run validate-setup.yml`)

## Automation Coverage

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Post-Merge Automation: Self-Configuring Repository Setup

## Overview
Create automated workflows and scripts that configure repository settings, integrations, and validations after the CI/CD modernization PR is merged, minimizing manual setup steps.

## Goal
Automate as much as possible so configurations "just kinda work" using GitHub Actions, APIs, and best practices.

## What CAN Be Automated

### 1. Repository Settings via GitHub API
- Branch protection rules
- Repository security settings
- Code scanning configurations
- Issue/PR templates
- Labels and milestones

### 2. Workflow-Based Setup
- Pre-commit hook installation instructions
- Development environment validation
- Configuration file validation
- Dependency cache warming

### 3. Integration Validation
- Check if Codecov is configured
- Verify PyPI trusted publishing setup
- Validate all secrets are present
- Test CI/CD pipeline integrity

## What REQUIRES Manual Setup (But We'll Guide)

### 1. External Service Tokens
- **Codecov:** Requires account sign-up and token generation
- **PyPI:** Requires account and trusted publishing configuration

### 2. GitHub Repository Secrets
- Must be added manually via UI or `gh` CLI

## Implementation

### Phase 1: Post-Merge Configuration Workflow

#### **File: `.github/workflows/post-merge-setup.yml`**

Create workflow that runs ONCE after the modernization PR is merged to configure repository settings:

```yaml
name: Post-Merge Repository Setup

on:
  workflow_dispatch: # Manual trigger
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  security-events: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  setup:
    # Only run if PR was merged (not just closed)
    if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    
    - name: Setup Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: '3.11'
    
    - name: Install GitHub CLI
      run: |
        type -p curl >/dev/null || (sudo apt update && sudo apt install curl -y)
        curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo dd of=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
        && sudo chmod go+r /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
        && echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list > /dev/null \
        && sudo apt update \
        && sudo apt install gh -y
    
    - name: Configure Branch Protection Rules
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      run: |
        echo "🔒 Setting up branch protection for main..."
        
        # Create branch protection rule
        gh api \
          --method PUT \
          -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
          /repos/${{ github.repository }}/branches/main/protection \
          -f required_status_checks='{"strict":true,"contexts":["CI / test (3.10)","CI / test (3.11)","CI / test (3.12)","CodeQL / Analyze (python)"]}' \
          -f enforce_admins=false \
          -f required_pull_request_reviews='{"dismissal_restrictions":{},"dismiss_stale_reviews":true,"require_code_owner_reviews":false,"required_approving_review_count":1}' \
          -f restrictions=null \
          -f required_linear_history=false \
          -f allow_force_pushes=false \
          -f allow_deletions=false \
          -f block_creations=false \
          -f required_conversation_resolution=true \
          || echo "⚠️  Branch protection may already exist or requires admin permissions"
    
    - name: Configure Repository Settings
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      run: |
        echo "⚙️  Configuring repository settings..."
        
        # Enable vulnerability alerts
        gh api \
          --method PUT \
          -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
          /repos/${{ github.repository }}/vulnerability-alerts \
          || echo "⚠️  Vulnerability alerts may already be enabled"
        
        # Enable automated security fixes (Dependabot)
        gh api \
          --method PUT \
          -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
          /repos/${{ github.repository }}/automated-security-fixes \
          || echo "⚠️  Automated security fixes may already be enabled"
        
        # Update repository settings
        gh api \
          --method PATCH \
          -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
          /repos/${{ github.repository }} \
          -f allow_squash_merge=true \
          -f allow_merge_commit=false \
          -f allow_rebase_merge=true \
          -f delete_branch_on_merge=true \
          -f allow_auto_merge=true \
          || ...

</details>

body:
Update wait event name list to use Postgres 18 latest, using REL_18_STABLE branch of today (as of https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/64893323925322d2236aaac111343768cf7dafa0/src/backend/utils/activity/wait_event_names.txt).

Here is some rules that I followed (which I also mentioned in the PR review comments but leaving here as well as a note):

* If the name is moved to the different type (e.g. moved to IPC from LWLock), do not create a new enum for it, but leave the comment that it moved in compact_activity_snapshot.proto
* If the name is changed (e.g. from PG17, it uses CamelCase except LWLock), put the alternate name in wait_event.json, but make sure the new name will be listed below the old one
  * This allows us to match with the old name for a backward compatibility, but show the new name in the UI

The source file I mainly used to update:

* https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/REL_18_STABLE/src/backend/utils/activity/wait_event_names.txt
  * Works well for any changes after PG17
* https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/8fba928fd78856712f69d96852f8061e77390fda/src/include/utils/wait_event.h
  * works well for any changes before PG17 (except LWLock)
* https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/1267d9862fc6a4f8cdc0ca38d1988b61f39da585/src/include/pgstat.h
  * in https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/a333476b925134f6185037eaff3424c07a9f466f, the pgstat.h file is moved to wait_event.h, so it's good to check any changes before that (except LWLock)
* https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/fa88928470b538c0ec0289e4d69ee12356c5a8ce/src/backend/storage/lmgr/lwlocknames.txt
* https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/e5da0fe3c22b34c4433f1729e88495554b5331ed/src/backend/storage/lmgr/lwlocknames.txt
  * works well for any changes before PG17 (for LWLock)
* https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/REL_18_STABLE/src/include/storage/lwlocklist.h
  * maybe it can pull some info/diff of LWLock that is not available in wait_event_names.txt

This fixes the bug of most of the LWLock type wait events not showing up in the pganalyze UI. This bug was happening because we were unable to understand the wait event like "ShmemIndex".

Moving forward, we should be only checking the history of https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/utils/activity/wait_event_names.txt, thanks to Michael-san 🙇
